title: IN WHICH IT IS SHOWN THAT PHILEAS FOGG GAINED NOTHING BY HIS TOUR AROUND THE WORLD, UNLESS IT WERE HAPPINESS
summary_hover: Fogg learns he miscounted a day, rushes to the Reform Club in time to win his wager, and marries Aouda.
summary_detail: Passepartout discovers that it is actually Saturday, not Sunday, and drags Fogg to the Reform Club, where Fogg arrives with minutes to spare and wins his twenty-thousand-pound wager. The chapter explains that by travelling constantly eastward Fogg unknowingly gained a full day, seeing the sun cross the meridian eighty times to London's seventy-nine. Though his winnings barely exceed his expenses, Fogg marries Aouda, whose suggestion of marriage had prompted the errand that revealed his error. In the end his real gain from the journey is happiness, not money.
